drug_identity.active_ingredient: Hyaluronic acid, Polyvinyl alcohol, Carboxymethylcellulose, Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, Petroleum, etc.
drug_identity.class: Tear Replacement and Ocular Lubricating Agents
drug_identity.off_label_note: Extra-label use in veterinary medicine for tear replacement, KCS, and corneal protection during anesthesia.

cyp_profile.pathway_evidence: Locally acting on the pre-corneal tear film. Systemic absorption is minimal.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Basic components include demulcents (soothing agents), emollients, inactive ingredients, and preservatives.

organ_burden_logic.note: Topical ophthalmic administration limits systemic exposure. Organ burden is negligible.

timing_profile.evidence: Acts locally and immediately upon instillation.

_ddi_note: Apply at least 5 minutes after other eye medications. Interactions with other topical ocular preparations may occur, leading to decreased efficacy or precipitate formation.

dosage_list.duration_note: Administer to affected eye(s) every 2-3 hours or as often as possible.
Do not use petroleum-based lubricants if combustion or intraocular contact may occur.
Administer to affected eye(s) every 2-3 hours or as often as possible.
Do not use petroleum-based lubricants if combustion or intraocular contact may occur.

contraindications.condition: Use of petroleum-based products during procedures with combustion risk (e.g., electrocautery, laser)
Use of petroleum-based products in penetrating corneal wounds (intraocular contact)

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Improves the quality (viscosity, osmolarity, retention time) of the precorneal tear film. Demulcents soothe and relieve inflammation, emollients protect tissues and stabilize the lipid layer.

species_notes.dog: Hyaluronic acid-containing preparations may accelerate the healing of corneal ulcers.
species_notes.cat: Hyaluronic acid-containing preparations may accelerate the healing of corneal ulcers.

dog.evidence: Preservative-free solutions are less likely to cause stinging or corneal damage with long-term use. Some preservatives (e.g., benzalkonium chloride) can cause epithelial cell damage.

cat.evidence: Preservative-free solutions are less likely to cause stinging or corneal damage with long-term use.

storage_and_forms.storage: Store at controlled room temperature (20°C-25°C [68°F-77°F]) away from moisture and sunlight. Do not freeze.

section_1_2_10.highlights: Used for temporary enhancement of tear film. Most are OTC human products. Preservative-free solutions are better for long-term use. Avoid petroleum-based products if combustion or intraocular contact is possible.
section_1_2_10.indications: Decreased tear production (KCS), increased tear evaporation, buphthalmos, lagophthalmos. Used to prevent corneal desiccation during sedation/anesthesia.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Administer drops frequently during the day, long-acting ointments at bedtime. If applying multiple ocular medications, apply lubricants last, at least 5 minutes after others. Avoid touching dropper tip to the eye.
